english.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for both needing something and needing to do something.

exampleSentences.english: I need to go to work today.
exampleSentences.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 jat6 jiu3 faan1 gung1

english.note: Use 要 as the all-purpose spoken way to say that someone is required to do something.

exampleSentences.english: You must remember to bring an umbrella, or you'll get soaked.
exampleSentences.traditional: 你要記得帶遮，唔係會濕晒。
exampleSentences.jyutping: nei5 jiu3 gei3 dak1 daai3 ze1 m4 hai6 wui5 sap1 saai3

english.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for saying that something is needed or that someone must do something.

exampleSentences.english: You require this form to be handed in today.
exampleSentences.jyutping: nei5 jiu3 gam1 jat6 gaau1 ni1 fan6 biu2

english.note: This is the all-purpose everyday choice for saying that someone must or needs to do something.

exampleSentences.english: I have to go to work tomorrow.
exampleSentences.jyutping: ngo5 ting1 jat6 jiu3 faan1 gung1

english.note: Use 要 when want means need, request, require, or be advised to do something.

exampleSentences.english: I want to take today off because I have something to do.
exampleSentences.jyutping: gam1 jat6 ngo5 jau5 si6 jiu3 cing2 gaa3

english.note: Use 要 when the duty sounds firm or close to an instruction rather than neutral advice.

exampleSentences.english: You ought to get to work on time tomorrow; don't be late again.
exampleSentences.traditional: 你聽日要準時返工，唔好再遲到。
exampleSentences.jyutping: nei5 ting1 jat6 jiu3 zeon2 si4 faan1 gung1 m4 hou2 zoi3 ci4 dou3
